text_blocks.snippet: A Health Savings Account (HSA) can be used to pay for a wide range of qualified medical expenses, including those for yourself, your spouse, and your dependents. These expenses can cover a variety of healthcare costs, including doctor visits, prescriptions, dental and vision care, and even certain over-the-counter medications.

list.snippet: Medical Expenses: Doctor visits, hospital stays, surgery, lab fees, X-rays, prescription drugs, and over-the-counter medications (with a prescription).
Dental Expenses: Routine checkups, cleanings, fillings, braces, and other dental procedures.
Vision Expenses: Eye exams, eyeglasses, contact lenses, and LASIK surgery.
Mental Health: Psychiatric care, therapy, and drug addiction treatment.
Other: Acupuncture, chiropractic care, ambulance services, artificial limbs, hearing aids, and more.

related_questions.snippet: Does HSA spending trigger an audit? And if your tax return contains unrelated IRS audit red flags, your risk for an HSA audit could increase.
